title: A gap caliper whose foot lands under a row label keeps its number off that label
goal: When you measure the space between two cards at a spot that sits below a row label, the number can jump up and land on top of that label. It should treat that row like any other row and keep the number off the text.
notes: Found while rendering options for a-caliper-boxed-in-by-two-full-width-rows-finds (temp/boxed-in/Render.swift, scene cards-left). ElementBounds.subjects(from:to:mode:in:luma:) at (330,417)->(330,450) returns only the whitespace band and the lower row; the upper row (96,322.5,1248,89) is missing, so MeasureLabelPlanner nudges the chip up to y 357.5..401.5, which covers the tail of the label. Likely the probe above the top foot hits the glyphs of the label and reads them as the element (too small, dropped by minElement) instead of the row. Compare x=700 where both rows come back.
acceptance: On the audit capture, a Gap caliper in the space between the two cards at x=330 (under the words Play sound on capture) lists the upper row among its subjects.
The number does not cover the label text there, verified with a rendered shot.
The gap sweep in the callout clearance tests fails if a foot under label text loses its row again.
